newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour decries "disappointing" trade figures.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour decries "disappointing" trade figures.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party said on Tuesday that latest official figures showing a widening trade gap poured cold water on the government's claims for the economy.

"Today's disappointing statistics show the trade gap widening both with the European Union countries and with the rest of the world," Labour's trade spokeswoman Margaret Beckett said. "They show once again that the Conservatives' general claims for the economy are grossly over-optimistic."
The government's claim to make Britain the enterprise centre of Europe was a "slogan without substance," she said.
Earlier on Tuesday, the Office for National Statistics said Britain's global trade deficit widened to 959 million pounds in November, from 680 million the month before.
Its deficit with European Union countries edged out to 260 million pounds from 227 million.
A Treasury spokesman focused on a three percent fall in import prices between October and November, saying that was good news for inflation.
The ONS also said that for 1996, Britain's trade shortfall with non-EU nations was estimated to total 9.0 billion pounds, up from 7.4 billion in 1995.

"In 1996, the UK will have recorded its 14th successive annual deficit in trade in goods -- deficits that the Chancellor complacently forecasts will continue to get bigger in 1997 and 1998," Beckett said.
